title: King's Lynn Tandoori named England's best curry restaurant at national awards
excerpt: The West Norfolk restaurant won the Best Restaurant Award at the Curry Life Awards in London, presented by BBC Breakfast's Jon Kay and Luxmy Gopal.
body:
• King's Lynn Tandoori in Wootton Road, King's Lynn, won the Best Restaurant Award at the Curry Life Awards in London, being named England's best curry restaurant in a national awards scheme.
  • The award was presented by BBC Breakfast presenters Jon Kay and Luxmy Gopal at the October 5, 2026 ceremony.
  • The restaurant opened in February 2019, weeks before the pandemic, and is run by manager Russel Islam with a team of around 10.
  • Judges praised its consistently high standards of food and service; Curry Life magazine has served the UK curry sector for 21 years.

A West Norfolk Indian restaurant has been named England's best curry restaurant in a national awards scheme. King's Lynn Tandoori, on Wootton Road, won the Best Restaurant Award at the Curry Life Awards in London, the ceremony reported by Local Free News on October 6, 2026.

Context & Background

The Curry Life Awards, run by the Curry Life trade magazine — a publication for the UK curry sector in its 21st year of operation — celebrate the country's Indian and Bangladeshi restaurants. King's Lynn Tandoori appears on the official Curry Life winners list as a Best Restaurant of the Year 2026, making it the national pick from a field spanning the UK.

The presentation carried star power: the award was handed over by BBC Breakfast presenters Jon Kay and Luxmy Gopal at the London ceremony. The restaurant's spokesperson called it "a fabulous evening, made even more special by receiving our award from" the two presenters, thanking customers, friends and the team.

Impact & Analysis

The judges' verdict focused on consistency rather than novelty: King's Lynn Tandoori "quickly established itself as one of the town's leading Indian restaurants," with "a team of around 10 staff, led by manager Russel Islam," delivering "a warm welcome and consistently high standards" of food and service.

That consistency story has a backstory. The restaurant opened in February 2019 — just weeks before the pandemic reshaped hospitality — and survived the industry's hardest years to reach its seventh anniversary. Manager Russel Islam thanked "everybody who has supported us for the last seven years," a reminder of how many neighbourhood curry houses closed while this one held on and grew.

Norfolk's curry scene is quietly competitive: a dozen of the county's Indian restaurants were finalists at the inaugural Southern Curry Awards 2026, and Downham Tandoori separately collected three honours there. For King's Lynn Tandoori, the national Curry Life title puts it above the county pack — the kind of recognition that fills tables for months.

Diaspora Angle

For the South Asian diaspora in Norfolk and beyond, the win is a neighbourhood story made national: the British curry house remains one of the diaspora's most visible contributions to British life, and awards like these are where the community's restaurants get their due. British-Indian diners passing through King's Lynn now know which kitchen the judges picked.

What's Next

The title gives the restaurant national bragging rights and a full order book to defend — the next test is living up to it. With the UK curry awards calendar now crowded with regional and national schemes, expect more of Norfolk's strong field to chase the same crown next year.
